name: Breakthrough Human Technologies
description: Questions covering: Printing Technology, Steam Power, Vaccination, Electric Lighting, Telephone...

questions.question: Which inventor is credited with introducing movable metal type printing to Europe in the mid-15th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Johannes Gutenberg is credited with developing a movable-metal-type printing system in Europe in the mid-15th century. Movable type had been used earlier in East Asia, including Bi Sheng's clay type; this question is specifically about its European introduction. His press helped make book production faster and more repeatable.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caxton was a later English printer, while Manutius and Schoeffer were important printers or publishers. Gutenberg is the figure associated with movable-metal-type printing in Europe.

questions.question: Which engineer is associated with major improvements to the steam engine?
questions.explanation_correct: James Watt is known for improving the steam engine, especially by increasing its efficiency. His enhancements helped drive the Industrial Revolution.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures also worked with steam or industrial machinery, but Watt is the one most specifically linked to major steam engine improvements. They are not the standard answer for this innovation.

questions.question: Who pioneered the first widely used smallpox vaccine?
questions.explanation_correct: Edward Jenner developed the first successful smallpox vaccine in the late 18th century. His work established the basis of modern immunization.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures made major contributions to medicine and microbiology, but they are not the pioneer associated with the smallpox vaccine. Their work belongs to different medical breakthroughs.

questions.question: Which inventor received U.S. Patent 223,898 for an improvement to the incandescent electric lamp?
questions.explanation_correct: Thomas Edison received U.S. Patent 223,898 for an electric-lamp improvement in 1880. Joseph Swan independently developed practical incandescent lamps, so the patent number makes this question specific to Edison.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Joseph Swan independently developed a practical incandescent lamp, while Tesla and Claude are associated with other electrical technologies. The patent named in the question was issued to Edison.

questions.question: Who received the landmark U.S. patent for transmitting speech electrically in 1876?
questions.explanation_correct: Alexander Graham Bell received U.S. Patent 174,465 for an improvement in telegraphy that covered a telephone. Bell and Elisha Gray both filed telephone-related papers on 14 February 1876, so this question identifies the patent recipient rather than claiming Bell was the only person working on voice transmission.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Elisha Gray filed a competing caveat on the same day, while Morse and Volta are associated with other communication and electrical technologies. The patent referenced here was granted to Bell.

questions.question: Which brothers made the first controlled, sustained flight of a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft in 1903?
questions.explanation_correct: The Wright brothers made a series of controlled, sustained flights in a powered, heavier-than-air aircraft at Kitty Hawk in 1903. The wording identifies the documented milestone without implying that no earlier powered flight attempts occurred.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Montgolfier brothers are associated with balloon flight, and the other teams worked on later aircraft. The Wrights made the 1903 controlled, sustained powered flights described here.

questions.question: Who discovered penicillin?
questions.explanation_correct: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when he observed its antibacterial effect. This discovery led to the development of modern antibiotics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists were important in microbiology and antibiotic development, but Fleming is the one who discovered penicillin. Their work came later or in different contexts.

questions.question: Which Bell Labs physicist is known as a co-inventor of the transistor?
questions.explanation_correct: William Shockley, John Bardeen, and Walter Brattain were the three members of the Bell Labs team who collectively received the Nobel Prize for the invention of the transistor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While all three were inventors, the question is better served by acknowledging them as a group to avoid factual ambiguity about who was 'the' sole inventor.

questions.question: In the field of computer science, which British polymath proposed the mathematical model of computation that bears his name?
questions.explanation_correct: Alan Turing formalized an abstract model of computation, now called a Turing machine, in his 1936 paper on computable numbers. The model remains central to the theory of computation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Alonzo Church and Kurt Gödel were contemporaries who worked on logic, but did not define this specific machine model.

questions.question: Who led the rocket engineering work behind Saturn V development?
questions.explanation_correct: Wernher von Braun played a leading role in developing the Saturn V rocket for NASA. His engineering work was crucial to the Apollo program.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are significant figures in rocketry and spaceflight, but von Braun is the one tied to Saturn V development. They are not the specific answer requested here.

questions.question: Which engineer demonstrated the first working integrated-circuit prototype at Texas Instruments in 1958?
questions.explanation_correct: Jack Kilby demonstrated a working integrated-circuit prototype at Texas Instruments in 1958. His hand-wired solid-circuit approach showed that active and passive components could be made from one piece of semiconductor, while Robert Noyce later developed the practical monolithic metal-over-oxide interconnection scheme.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Robert Noyce developed the planar monolithic approach for practical production, while Bardeen and Turing are associated with other breakthroughs. Kilby demonstrated the 1958 working prototype at Texas Instruments.

questions.question: Which agency initiated and funded ARPANET while it was called ARPA?
questions.explanation_correct: The Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA) initiated and funded ARPANET in the 1960s. The agency was renamed the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) in 1972, after ARPANET began operating.
questions.explanation_incorrect: NASA, NSF, and the FCC did not initiate ARPANET. DARPA is the agency's later name; it was called ARPA when the network project began.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation_correct: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN. He developed the core ideas of URLs, HTTP, and HTML.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are major figures in computing and the internet, but they are not the inventor of the Web.

questions.question: Which tool is widely used for precise DNA editing?
questions.explanation_correct: CRISPR-Cas9 is a gene-editing system that can target and modify DNA with high precision. It has become a standard tool in molecular biology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are important biotechnology techniques, but they are not gene-editing systems.

questions.question: What is the name of the 'Imitation Game' used to determine if a computer can exhibit behavior indistinguishable from a person?
questions.explanation_correct: The test was introduced in a 1950 paper as a way to answer the question 'Can machines think?'
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Loebner Prize is a competition based on the test, but it is not the name of the test itself.

questions.question: Which French mathematician invented the Pascaline, an early mechanical adding machine, in the 1640s?
questions.explanation_correct: Blaise Pascal designed the Pascaline in the 1640s to help his father with arithmetic. Earlier calculator designs, including Wilhelm Schickard's, are known, so Pascal is credited here with this named adding machine rather than the first mechanical calculator of any kind.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Leibniz and Babbage designed other calculating machines, and Jacquard developed a programmable loom. The question asks specifically about Pascal's adding machine, the Pascaline.

questions.question: Who discovered X-rays?
questions.explanation_correct: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895. His discovery transformed medical imaging and physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are renowned in physics and chemistry, but they are not credited with discovering X-rays.

questions.question: Who developed the first polio vaccine?
questions.explanation_correct: Jonas Salk developed the first successful polio vaccine, which used an inactivated virus. It was a major breakthrough in public health.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are associated with vaccines or microbiology, but they are not the developer of the first polio vaccine.

questions.question: Which inventor is most associated with establishing practical wireless telegraphy, including the 1901 transatlantic signal?
questions.explanation_correct: Guglielmo Marconi developed commercial wireless telegraphy and is associated with the 1901 transatlantic signal. The history of radio also includes foundational work by Hertz and contributions from Tesla and others, so Marconi is not presented as its sole inventor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Hertz demonstrated electromagnetic waves, and Tesla and Bell made important related contributions. Marconi is the figure associated here with establishing practical wireless telegraphy and the transatlantic signal.

questions.question: Who led the team that achieved the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in 1942?
questions.explanation_correct: Enrico Fermi led the team that brought Chicago Pile-1 to criticality at the University of Chicago on 2 December 1942, achieving the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists made important contributions to nuclear physics and the Manhattan Project, but Fermi led the experiment that achieved the first controlled, self-sustaining chain reaction.

questions.question: Which of these researchers is credited with introducing the concept of 'packet switching' at the National Physical Laboratory in the UK?
questions.explanation_correct: Donald Davies coined the term 'packet switching' while researching at the National Physical Laboratory in the United Kingdom. Paul Baran independently developed similar ideas in the United States around the same time.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While Paul Baran is a co-inventor of the concept, the question specifically focuses on the researcher associated with the NPL. Vint Cerf and Claude Shannon contributed to networking and information theory, respectively.

questions.question: Which German biotechnology company partnered with Pfizer to develop the COVID-19 vaccine later branded Comirnaty?
questions.explanation_correct: BioNTech partnered with Pfizer to develop BNT162b2, later branded Comirnaty. The question identifies the German biotechnology partner; Pfizer was also a co-developer and commercial partner.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Moderna developed a separate mRNA vaccine, Pfizer was BioNTech's partner, and AstraZeneca's vaccine used a different platform.

questions.question: Which space agency led the Apollo program?
questions.explanation_correct: NASA managed and executed the Apollo program, including the Moon landings. It was the U.S. civilian agency responsible for the mission series.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are space agencies as well, but they did not lead Apollo. Apollo was a U.S. program carried out by NASA.

questions.question: Which company introduced the Macintosh?
questions.explanation_correct: Apple introduced the Macintosh in 1984, helping popularize the graphical user interface in personal computing. The Macintosh became one of the company’s signature products.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other companies are major computing firms, but they did not introduce the Macintosh. Their landmark products were different systems and platforms.

questions.question: Which U.S. institution played a central leadership role in the public Human Genome Project?
questions.explanation_correct: The National Institutes of Health played a central role in the public Human Genome Project, jointly coordinated with the U.S. Department of Energy. NIH’s National Human Genome Research Institute led the project’s biomedical research effort.
questions.explanation_incorrect: NSF, CDC, and FDA were not the lead agencies for the public Human Genome Project. NIH and the Department of Energy shared central leadership roles.

questions.question: What term refers to the machine learning architecture introduced by Vaswani and colleagues?
questions.explanation_correct: The Transformer is the neural network architecture introduced by Vaswani and colleagues in their influential 2017 paper. It became the basis for many modern language and generative models.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are legitimate machine learning models, but they are not the architecture introduced by Vaswani and colleagues. They belong to different model families.

questions.question: Which process is used to synthesize ammonia at industrial scale?
questions.explanation_correct: The Haber-Bosch process converts nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia on an industrial scale. It revolutionized fertilizer production and modern agriculture.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are industrial or chemical processes, but they are not the ammonia synthesis method asked for. Each is associated with a different material or application.

questions.question: Who is credited as the co-inventor of the planar integrated circuit at Fairchild?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Noyce is credited with co-inventing the planar integrated circuit at Fairchild. His work helped launch the modern semiconductor industry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Jack Kilby is also associated with the integrated circuit, but in a different implementation. Gordon Moore and William Shockley were important semiconductor pioneers, but not the co-inventor asked for here.

questions.question: Which inventor developed the polyphase AC system adopted by George Westinghouse for power generation and distribution?
questions.explanation_correct: Nikola Tesla developed patents for a polyphase alternating-current system that George Westinghouse licensed and helped commercialize. The question distinguishes Tesla's technical work from Westinghouse's major role in bringing AC systems to market.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Edison promoted direct-current systems, Westinghouse commercialized AC technology, and Faraday made foundational discoveries in electromagnetism. Tesla developed the polyphase system identified here.

questions.question: Who is recognized as a pioneer of antiseptic surgery?
questions.explanation_correct: Joseph Lister pioneered antiseptic surgery by introducing methods to reduce infection during operations. His practices transformed surgical safety and outcomes.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are important medical or scientific figures, but they are not the pioneer of antiseptic surgery named in the blueprint. Their work lies in related but different fields.

questions.question: Which Chinese inventor developed an early movable-type printing method using clay type?
questions.explanation_correct: Bi Sheng is credited with creating an early movable-type printing system in China during the Song dynasty. His work preceded later European movable-type printing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are associated with different printing-era innovations or unrelated inventions. They did not originate the early clay movable-type method.

questions.question: Who was the chief engineer of the Stockton and Darlington Railway when Locomotion No. 1 entered service in 1825?
questions.explanation_correct: George Stephenson was chief engineer of the Stockton and Darlington Railway and drove Locomotion No. 1 on its opening day in 1825. The locomotive was made by Robert Stephenson and Company; some sources associate its design with Timothy Hackworth, so this question asks about the railway’s chief engineer rather than sole authorship of the locomotive.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Trevithick built earlier experimental locomotives, Brunel was a later railway engineer, and Watt improved steam engines. George Stephenson was the Stockton and Darlington Railway’s chief engineer in 1825.

questions.question: Which English noblewoman promoted smallpox inoculation after observing the practice abroad?
questions.explanation_correct: Lady Mary Wortley Montagu introduced and advocated variolation in Britain after seeing the practice in the Ottoman Empire. Her efforts helped spread smallpox inoculation in Europe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are associated with nursing or medicine, but not with introducing smallpox inoculation in Britain. They did not play the same historical role.

questions.question: Which Italian physicist independently demonstrated an induction motor using a rotating magnetic field in the 1880s?
questions.explanation_correct: Galileo Ferraris demonstrated an induction motor based on a rotating magnetic field and published his work in 1888. Nikola Tesla independently developed a related motor and polyphase system around the same period, so Ferraris is not described as the sole inventor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tesla independently developed a related induction motor, while Faraday and Siemens are associated with other electrical advances. The question specifies Ferraris’s Italian work.

questions.question: What name did Antonio Meucci give to his early voice-communication device?
questions.explanation_correct: Antonio Meucci called his voice-communication apparatus the teletrofono. His work is part of the telephone’s contested early history, but the name of his device is a specific, verifiable detail.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The harmonic telegraph was associated with Bell’s early work, the photophone transmitted sound using light, and the phonograph recorded sound. Meucci called his apparatus the teletrofono.

questions.question: Which aviation pioneer is best known for early successful helicopter designs?
questions.explanation_correct: Igor Sikorsky developed some of the first practical helicopters and is a major figure in rotary-wing aviation. His aircraft helped establish the modern helicopter.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are associated with fixed-wing flight, record-setting aviation, or other aircraft innovations. They are not chiefly known for helicopter pioneering.

questions.question: Which physician led the medical development of penicillin for clinical use?
questions.explanation_correct: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain led the Oxford team that purified penicillin and demonstrated its therapeutic potential, building on Alexander Fleming’s earlier discovery. Florey led the clinical-development and production effort.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fleming discovered penicillin, and Chain was a key collaborator in the Oxford team. The physician asked for here is Florey, who led the clinical-development effort.

questions.question: Who co-invented the MOSFET with Dawon Kahng at Bell Labs?
questions.explanation_correct: Mohamed Atalla and Dawon Kahng jointly demonstrated and patented the MOSFET at Bell Labs in 1959–1960. The device became a central component of modern electronics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bardeen, Kilby, and Shockley made major contributions to transistor and integrated-circuit technology, but the MOSFET was jointly developed by Atalla and Kahng.

questions.question: Which protocol became the foundational transfer protocol for the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation_correct: HTTP is the protocol used for transferring web pages and related resources on the World Wide Web. It became the web's core communication standard.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are network protocols, but they serve different functions such as file transfer, email, or lower-level transport. They are not the web protocol in question.

questions.question: Which American engineer is recognized as a pioneer of the liquid-fuel rocket?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Goddard built and launched some of the earliest successful liquid-fuel rockets. His experiments helped establish modern rocketry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are major rocket theorists or later rocketry figures. They are not the specific pioneer most closely tied to early liquid-fuel rocket flights.

questions.question: Who developed the first practical clinical CT scanner at EMI?
questions.explanation_correct: Godfrey Hounsfield developed the first practical clinical CT scanner at EMI. Allan Cormack independently provided important mathematical foundations for computed tomography; both shared the 1979 Nobel Prize for its development.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are associated with other fields of science and technology. Cormack made a separate foundational contribution to CT, but Hounsfield developed the practical scanner asked about here.

questions.question: Which physicist is known for discovering the neutron?
questions.explanation_correct: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932. This was a major advance in nuclear physics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are known for artificial intelligence, printing, and steam transportation rather than particle discovery.

questions.question: Which American researcher independently developed packet-switching concepts for distributed communications?
questions.explanation_correct: Paul Baran developed packet-switching concepts for resilient, distributed communications in the United States. Donald Davies independently developed packet switching at the UK’s National Physical Laboratory and coined the term.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are associated with medicine, electrical power, or automotive engineering. Davies also independently developed packet switching, but the American researcher described here is Paul Baran.

questions.question: Who invented the polymerase chain reaction (PCR)?
questions.explanation_correct: Kary Mullis invented PCR, a technique for amplifying DNA. It became foundational in molecular biology and diagnostics.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are linked to medical imaging, physics, and printing, not DNA amplification.

questions.question: Which researcher co-developed Boltzmann machines and helped revive deep neural-network research?
questions.explanation_correct: Geoffrey Hinton co-developed Boltzmann machines with Terrence Sejnowski and later made influential contributions to deep neural networks. These are concrete contributions behind his recognition as a deep-learning pioneer.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are associated with networking, transportation, and medicine. Hinton’s work on Boltzmann machines and deep neural networks is the subject of the question.

questions.question: Who invented lithography?
questions.explanation_correct: Alois Senefelder invented lithography in the late 18th century. The technique became an important printing method.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are associated with vaccination, nuclear physics, and biotechnology, not printing processes.

questions.question: Which engineer’s North River Steamboat, popularly called the Clermont, began commercial service on the Hudson in 1807?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Fulton developed and operated the North River Steamboat, popularly known as the Clermont, which began commercial service on the Hudson River in 1807. Fulton helped make steamboat transport commercially viable; he did not invent the steamboat in general.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are notable inventors and scientists, but they are not associated with Fulton’s North River Steamboat service.

questions.question: Who developed the first rabies vaccine?
questions.explanation_correct: Louis Pasteur developed the first rabies vaccine. His research was a landmark in immunology and preventive medicine.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names belong to physics, printing, and electrical engineering rather than vaccine development.

questions.question: Which engineer developed the three-phase induction motor that became important in industrial AC power?
questions.explanation_correct: Mikhail Dolivo-Dobrovolsky developed practical three-phase AC motors and power systems in the late 19th century. The question specifies the three-phase industrial motor, distinguishing his contribution from Tesla’s and Ferraris’s independent work on induction motors.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures contributed to different areas of science and engineering. The three-phase induction motor and associated system described here are linked to Dolivo-Dobrovolsky.

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing the Motorwagen, often regarded as the first practical automobile?
questions.explanation_correct: Karl Benz patented the three-wheeled Motorwagen in 1886, often cited as the first practical automobile. His work is a milestone in automotive history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are associated with artificial intelligence, microbiology, and networking rather than the invention of the automobile.

questions.question: Which scientist, working with Pierre Curie, announced the discovery of radium in 1898?
questions.explanation_correct: Marie and Pierre Curie announced the discovery of radium in 1898 after studying pitchblende. This wording credits Marie while making clear that the discovery was collaborative.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists made major contributions to science, but the 1898 discovery of radium was announced by Marie and Pierre Curie.

questions.question: Who designed the first successful monoplane crossing of the English Channel?
questions.explanation_correct: Louis Blériot designed and flew the first successful monoplane to cross the English Channel in 1909. This flight became a landmark in aviation history.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other aviators were pioneers in flight, but they are not the designer associated with that specific Channel crossing.

questions.question: Who publicly demonstrated a working mechanical television system in London in 1926?
questions.explanation_correct: John Logie Baird publicly demonstrated a working mechanical television system in 1926. Electronic television was developed separately by pioneers such as Philo Farnsworth.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Farnsworth and Zworykin worked on electronic television, while Blumlein contributed to television and sound technology. Baird is associated with the 1926 mechanical-system demonstration.

questions.question: Who filed a British patent application for a turbojet engine in 1930?
options: J. A. J. B. de Havilland
questions.explanation_correct: Frank Whittle filed a British patent application for a turbojet engine in 1930. Hans von Ohain independently developed a jet engine in Germany, so Whittle is identified here by the specific British patent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Von Ohain independently developed a German jet engine, while the other figures worked in other areas of aviation and rocketry. The 1930 British patent was Whittle’s.

questions.question: Who created the World Wide Web's first browser-editor?
questions.explanation_correct: WorldWideWeb was the first browser-editor for the World Wide Web, created by Tim Berners-Lee. It later became known as Nexus.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are later web browsers, but they were not the first browser-editor.

questions.question: Who invented the key echo-planar method used in magnetic resonance imaging?
questions.explanation_correct: Peter Mansfield pioneered echo-planar imaging, a key MRI technique. His work greatly improved the speed of magnetic resonance imaging.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other scientists are important in imaging and medicine, but they are not the inventor of this specific MRI method.

questions.question: What was the name of the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born at the Roslin Institute in 1996?
questions.explanation_correct: Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell. A Roslin Institute and PPL Therapeutics team led by Ian Wilmut created her; Keith Campbell made an important contribution to the nuclear-transfer work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Megan and Morag were cloned from embryonic cells, and Polly was another genetically modified sheep. Dolly was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

questions.question: Who led the first handheld mobile phone demonstration?
questions.explanation_correct: Martin Cooper led the first handheld mobile phone demonstration at Motorola in 1973. This event is a milestone in mobile communications.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other inventors are famous in communications history, but they were not responsible for the first handheld mobile phone demonstration.

questions.question: Who was the chief designer of Sputnik 1?
questions.explanation_correct: Sergei Korolev was the chief designer behind Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite. He played a central role in early Soviet space technology.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures were important in Soviet space efforts, but they were not the chief designer of Sputnik 1.

questions.question: Who coined the term artificial intelligence?
questions.explanation_correct: John McCarthy used the term “artificial intelligence” in the 1955 proposal for the Dartmouth summer research project, held in 1956. He is widely credited with coining the name for the emerging field.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other pioneers helped develop computing and AI, but they did not coin the term.

questions.question: Which East Asian inventor is credited with improving papermaking in the Han dynasty?
questions.explanation_correct: Cai Lun is traditionally credited with major improvements to papermaking in Han China. His work helped standardize a more practical paper production method.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Chinese historical figures known for different inventions or scholarly contributions, not papermaking. They are not the correct inventor here.

questions.question: Which locomotive pioneer built an early steam engine capable of hauling a train on rails?
questions.explanation_correct: Richard Trevithick built one of the earliest steam locomotives and demonstrated steam traction on rails. He is a key figure in early railway development.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The others are associated with railways, steam engineering, or infrastructure, but not that specific pioneering locomotive. They do not match the clue.

questions.question: What was the pre-19th-century smallpox prevention method that involved deliberate exposure to material from a mild case?
questions.explanation_correct: Variolation was an early smallpox prevention practice that exposed a person to smallpox material to induce immunity. It predates Jenner’s cowpox-based vaccination.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vaccination used material from cowpox to protect against smallpox, quarantine separated people to limit transmission, and antisepsis prevents infection. The historic deliberate-exposure practice was variolation.

questions.question: Which current system transmits power through periodic reversal of direction?
questions.explanation_correct: Alternating current changes direction periodically and became the basis for modern long-distance power distribution. It is the system associated with major electrical power networks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are not the standard power-delivery system described here. They either do not reverse direction or are not recognized system names in this context.

questions.question: Which inventor is credited with the first automated telephone switching system?
questions.explanation_correct: Almon Strowger invented the automatic telephone exchange, reducing the need for human operators. His system was an important step in telephone network automation.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures were important in communications or electronics, but not for inventing automatic switching. They do not fit the clue.

questions.question: Which German engineer is associated with the co-invention of the first practical jet engine?
questions.explanation_correct: Hans von Ohain independently co-invented a practical jet engine in Germany. He is closely linked to early jet propulsion development.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options include another jet pioneer, a rocketry engineer, and an aircraft designer. They are not the intended answer for this clue.

questions.question: What was the first widely used sulfa drug?
questions.explanation_correct: Prontosil was the first sulfonamide drug to be widely used and marked a major advance in antimicrobial therapy. It was an early breakthrough before penicillin became dominant.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are a different antibiotic, a later antibiotic, and a pain reliever. They do not match the first sulfa drug.

questions.question: Which two chemists provided experimental evidence for uranium fission in 1938?
questions.explanation_correct: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann found barium among the products of bombarding uranium, providing key experimental evidence for nuclear fission. Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch supplied the physical interpretation and the term “fission.”
questions.explanation_incorrect: Meitner and Frisch interpreted the result theoretically, while Fermi, Szilard, Rutherford, and Chadwick made other nuclear discoveries. Hahn and Strassmann provided the experimental evidence asked about here.

questions.question: Which Bell Labs engineer co-invented the MOSFET with Mohamed Atalla?
questions.explanation_correct: Dawon Kahng co-invented the MOSFET with Mohamed Atalla at Bell Labs. The pair demonstrated the device in 1960, and MOSFETs later became essential to integrated circuits.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are famous semiconductor pioneers, but the MOSFET was jointly developed at Bell Labs by Kahng and Atalla.

questions.question: What was the name of the Soviet and Russian modular space station?
questions.explanation_correct: Mir was the Soviet and Russian modular space station that served as a long-duration orbital laboratory. It is the station name asked for here.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are other space stations from different programs or eras. They do not match the Soviet and Russian modular station.

questions.question: Which research lab is associated with the development of the graphical user interface that influenced personal computing?
questions.explanation_correct: Xerox PARC was the Palo Alto research center where key GUI concepts for personal computing were developed. Its work influenced later commercial computer interfaces.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are research labs, but they are not the one most closely associated with the early graphical interface work described here.

questions.question: Which physical phenomenon enables an ultrasound transducer to convert electrical energy into sound waves and back?
questions.explanation_correct: Piezoelectricity is the effect used in ultrasound transducers to generate and detect sound waves. It allows certain materials to change shape when electricity is applied and produce electricity when mechanically stressed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options describe different physical effects and are not the basis of standard ultrasound imaging hardware.

questions.question: Which mobile communications standard is a fourth-generation system widely deployed for high-speed data?
questions.explanation_correct: LTE, or Long Term Evolution, is a major 4G mobile communications standard designed for high data throughput and low latency. It became a common basis for modern cellular networks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are earlier or different cellular standards, not the one asked for here.

questions.question: Which molecular feature was used in early gene-targeting tools before CRISPR became dominant?
questions.explanation_correct: Zinc fingers are DNA-binding protein motifs used in zinc finger nucleases and related gene-editing tools. They were an important predecessor to CRISPR-based editing systems.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other choices are real biological terms, but they are not the gene-editing precursor specified in the question.

questions.question: Which trio co-authored the influential 1986 Nature paper on learning representations by back-propagating errors?
options: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams
questions.answer: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams
questions.explanation_correct: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams co-authored the 1986 Nature paper that described using back-propagation to train networks of neuron-like units. Earlier work on the method existed, so the question identifies the authors of this influential paper rather than claiming they invented back-propagation outright.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Turing, Hinton alone, and Hopfield are associated with important but different contributions. Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams jointly authored the specific 1986 paper named in the question.

questions.question: Who is credited with inventing movable metal type in Korea?
questions.explanation_correct: Choe Yun-ui is associated with early movable metal type in Korea. His work predates Gutenberg’s later European printing innovations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are historical Korean or printing-related names, but they are not the inventor named in the prompt.

questions.question: Who developed the practical steam turbine that became important in power generation and marine propulsion?
questions.explanation_correct: Charles Parsons developed the practical steam turbine in the late 19th century. His design became crucial for efficient electricity generation and marine propulsion.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other inventors are associated with engines, but not with the practical steam turbine specified here.

questions.question: Who is credited with developing the fluorescent lamp?
questions.explanation_correct: Edmund Germer is credited with developing the fluorescent lamp and related high-pressure mercury vapor lighting technology. His work helped make efficient fluorescent illumination practical.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other inventors are associated with electrical or lighting history, but not with the development of the fluorescent lamp. Their breakthroughs were in different types of lighting or electrical systems.

questions.question: Which inventor developed the Audion vacuum tube, later used to amplify weak telephone signals?
questions.explanation_correct: Lee de Forest developed the Audion, a grid-controlled vacuum tube that was later adapted to amplify weak telephone currents and support long-distance calls.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Strowger is associated with automatic telephone switching, Bell with the telephone and photophone, and Marconi with wireless telegraphy. De Forest developed the Audion amplifier.

questions.question: Who is credited with developing the single main rotor configuration used in helicopters?
questions.explanation_correct: Igor Sikorsky is widely credited with pioneering the practical single main rotor helicopter configuration. His designs helped establish the modern helicopter layout.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are associated with aircraft design or flight history, but not this helicopter configuration. They did not pioneer the standard single-rotor helicopter.

questions.question: Which researcher isolated streptomycin in Selman Waksman’s Rutgers laboratory in 1943?
questions.explanation_correct: Albert Schatz isolated streptomycin in 1943 while working in Selman Waksman’s laboratory at Rutgers. Waksman supervised the broader soil-microbe research program and received the 1952 Nobel Prize, but the question asks who isolated the compound.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fleming, Pasteur, and Koch made other important contributions to microbiology. Schatz isolated streptomycin in Waksman’s laboratory; the subsequent credit and Nobel recognition involved both researchers’ roles.

questions.question: Which company released the first commercially produced microprocessor in 1971?
questions.explanation_correct: The Intel 4004 was released in 1971 as the world's first commercially available microprocessor.
questions.explanation_incorrect: While TI and Motorola are industry giants, they did not release the first commercial microprocessor.

questions.question: What pretraining objective teaches BERT to predict tokens deliberately masked in its input text?
questions.explanation_correct: BERT is pretrained with a masked-language-model objective: selected input tokens are hidden, and the model learns to predict them using surrounding context. It also used a next-sentence prediction objective in the original paper.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Autoregressive next-token prediction is used by other language models, while image denoising and tree search are different tasks. BERT’s distinctive token-reconstruction objective is masked language modeling.

questions.question: Which NASA program utilized the first reusable orbital spacecraft?
questions.explanation_correct: NASA’s Space Shuttle was the first reusable crewed spacecraft system designed to carry an orbiter into Earth orbit and return it for later flights. The orbiter was reused; the external tank was not.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Apollo and Gemini used spacecraft that were not reflown after their missions, and Soyuz descends in a recoverable but non-reusable capsule. The Shuttle orbiter was designed for repeated orbital missions.

questions.question: Which imaging technique is based on nuclear magnetic resonance?
questions.explanation_correct: MRI uses nuclear magnetic resonance principles to generate detailed images of internal structures. It is especially valuable for soft tissue imaging.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options use X-rays, sound waves, or radioactive tracers. They do not rely on nuclear magnetic resonance.

questions.question: Which COVID-19 vaccine brand did the UK MHRA first authorize for use, on 2 December 2020?
questions.explanation_correct: The UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine on 2 December 2020. It was later branded Comirnaty; the authority and date make the first-authorization claim specific.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options were authorized later in the UK or use non-mRNA platforms. Comirnaty was the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine authorized first by the MHRA.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for domain name resolution?
questions.explanation_correct: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses. It is the core protocol for domain name resolution.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other protocols handle web transfer, file transfer, or email delivery. They do not resolve domain names.

questions.question: What is the site of the first self-sustaining nuclear reactor?
questions.explanation_correct: Chicago Pile-1 achieved the first controlled self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in 1942. It was built under Enrico Fermi's leadership.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other sites are associated with nuclear reactors or accidents, but not the first self-sustaining reactor. They came later or served different roles.

questions.question: Which type of transistor is used in modern integrated circuits?
questions.explanation_correct: MOSFETs are the dominant transistor type in modern integrated circuits. Their scalability made large-scale integration practical.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are different electronic devices or older transistor types. They are not the standard transistor used in modern ICs.

questions.question: Which printer established the first printing press in England, at Westminster, around 1476?
questions.explanation_correct: William Caxton established England’s first printing press at Westminster around 1476, after learning the trade in continental Europe. Johannes Gutenberg is associated with the earlier European movable-metal-type press.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gutenberg is associated with introducing movable metal type to Europe, Mergenthaler invented the Linotype machine, and Morison was a typographer. Caxton established the first English press at Westminster.

questions.question: Which animal disease did Edward Jenner use in his 1796 experiment that helped protect against smallpox?
questions.explanation_correct: Edward Jenner inoculated James Phipps with material from a cowpox lesion in 1796 and later showed protection against smallpox. This is distinct from variolation, which exposed a person to smallpox material.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Measles, rabies, and polio are unrelated diseases here. Jenner’s experiment used cowpox material, the basis of the term vaccination.

questions.question: What was the name of Alexander Graham Bell and Charles Sumner Tainter’s device for transmitting speech on a beam of light?
questions.explanation_correct: Bell and Tainter named their light-based voice-transmission device the photophone. In 1880 Bell reported transmitting articulate speech using sunlight and a light-sensitive selenium receiver.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names refer to different communication or sound technologies. The Bell-Tainter device that transmitted speech using light was the photophone.

questions.question: Who designed the Analytical Engine in computing?
questions.explanation_correct: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, a proposed mechanical general-purpose computer. It is considered a foundational concept in the history of computing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are central to computing history, but they did not design the Analytical Engine. Their work came later or focused on theoretical or programming contributions.

questions.question: Which inventor demonstrated a fully electronic television system using an image dissector in 1927?
questions.explanation_correct: Philo Farnsworth demonstrated an all-electronic television system using his image dissector in 1927. This distinguishes his work from John Logie Baird’s mechanical television demonstrations.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Baird is associated with mechanical television, while RCA and David Sarnoff were central to commercial television development. Farnsworth demonstrated the electronic image-dissection system described here.

questions.question: Which aircraft became the world’s first operational jet fighter?
questions.explanation_correct: The German Messerschmitt Me 262 became the world’s first operational jet fighter. The Heinkel He 178 was the first aircraft to fly under turbojet power, a different milestone.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The He 178 was an experimental jet aircraft, while the Gloster E.28/39 and Bell P-59 were development aircraft. The Me 262 was the first operational jet fighter.

questions.question: Which scientist is known as an ultrasound imaging pioneer in medical imaging?
questions.explanation_correct: Ian Donald was a major pioneer in using ultrasound for medical diagnosis, especially obstetrics. His work helped establish ultrasound imaging as a clinical tool.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other figures are landmark names in medical imaging, but not in ultrasound. Röntgen is associated with X-rays, while Hounsfield and Cormack are associated with CT.

questions.question: Which physicist filed a 1934 British patent application describing a neutron-induced chain reaction?
questions.explanation_correct: Leo Szilard filed a British patent application in June 1934 describing a neutron-induced chain reaction. The patent was published in 1936 after being assigned to the British Admiralty; Enrico Fermi later led the team that achieved the first controlled, self-sustaining reaction at Chicago Pile-1 in 1942.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fermi led the first controlled reactor experiment, while Oppenheimer and Bohr made other contributions to nuclear physics. Szilard filed the patent application for the chain-reaction idea described here.

questions.question: Which protocol family is associated with Internet communication?
questions.explanation_correct: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that underpins Internet communication. It defines how data is packetized, addressed, transmitted, and received across networks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other options are Internet-related protocols, but each serves a narrower function than the protocol family asked for here. They are not the foundational suite specified by the blueprint.

questions.question: Which two scientists introduced the hybridoma technique for producing monoclonal antibodies in 1975?
questions.explanation_correct: Georges Köhler and César Milstein introduced hybridoma technology in 1975, enabling continuous production of monoclonal antibodies with a specified target. Both shared the 1984 Nobel Prize with Niels Jerne for related immunological work.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mullis and Berg are associated with PCR and recombinant DNA, Watson and Crick with the DNA double-helix model, and Jerne with immunological theory. Köhler and Milstein introduced the hybridoma technique.
